analysis: What changed vs the 5:00 AM brief: the premarket story shifted from the AI-infrastructure beats themselves to how strictly the market is grading them. Seagate beat on EPS ($7.68 vs $7.42 expected), revenue (+60%+ year over year to $4.23B) and guidance — and still fell 2.5-3.3% premarket after a ~150% run this year. Robinhood went the other way on a genuine miss: crypto revenue down 55% to $120M dragged EPS below estimates, sending shares down 6-8%. That pair, landing an hour before the open, is the cleanest read on today's tape: beats are being sold when the run is already priced in, misses are being punished. Futures barely moved in the last hour (S&P +0.1% to +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.5% to +0.4%), so the open itself is still a holding pattern for the two real events — Microsoft and Alphabet after the close, and the Fed at 2:00 p.m. ET, where December hike odds have firmed to 86% per CME FedWatch via Investopedia, up from ~75% in the 5 AM read. Signal: the AI-infrastructure earnings chain (SK Hynix memory, Vertiv cooling, GE Vernova power, Seagate storage) is beating almost uniformly — the demand evidence is broad. Noise: single-stock premarket percentages, the still-unconfirmed OpenAI-TPU report and Houthi refinery claim, and any pre-read of Warsh's press conference.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures mixed into the open: Dow futures -0.2%, S&P 500 futures +0.2%, Nasdaq futures +0.4% in recent trading, per Investopedia — little changed from the 5 AM read. The 10-year yield sits at 5.01%, WTI crude up 2% at $101.75, gold slightly lower at $4,060, bitcoin at $81,300, up from Tuesday's low of $79,300.
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat-to-mixed open into a Fed day with two megacap prints after the close — the tape is waiting, not leading.

headlines.headline: Seagate fell 2.5% premarket (Barron's/Mondeum put it at -3.3%) despite beating: fiscal Q1 adjusted EPS $7.68 vs $7.42 expected, revenue up over 60% year over year to $4.23B vs $4.14B expected, and current-quarter guidance ahead of the Street. Shares were up almost 150% for the year through Tuesday's close.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that still sells off after a huge run — the strict-grading theme from Tuesday carries into today, and it sets the bar for tonight's Microsoft and Alphabet prints.

headlines.headline: Robinhood fell 6% premarket (Reuters/Barron's put it at 7-8%) after Q3 earnings missed: revenue rose 12% year over year to $1.42B, in line with consensus, but adjusted EPS of $0.60 missed as expenses climbed; crypto revenue plunged 55% to $120M. Agentic trading accounts more than doubled to about 200,000, driving over $1.6B in volume.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuine miss, not just profit-taking — crypto weakness is now a visible drag on a retail-trading bellwether, and it fits bitcoin's ~28% slide over three months.

headlines.headline: Alphabet rose about 1.2% premarket ahead of its Q3 print after the close (consensus roughly $128B revenue, about $2.94-3.03 EPS, Google Cloud near $29.15B); Microsoft slipped about 0.3% ahead of fiscal Q1 after the close (consensus roughly $90.6B revenue, about $4.71-4.73 EPS, Azure growth near 44.8%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The day's two biggest prints are both cloud stories — Google Cloud and Azure growth, plus AI capex commentary, matter more than headline EPS after Seagate's sell-the-beat.

headlines.headline: The Fed decision lands at 2:00 p.m. ET with Chair Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; traders price less than a 10% chance of a hike today, while December hike odds are now at 86% per CME FedWatch, up from about 75% in the earlier read.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is priced in, so December guidance is the trade — and the firming December odds plus oil back above $101 keep the hawkish-steer risk live.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Vertiv rose about 16% premarket on its Q3 blowout (EPS $2.21 vs $1.82 expected, revenue +60.8% to $4.31B, Q4 guide above consensus); GE Vernova beat and raised (orders up 96% to $29B); SK Hynix jumped about 7.5% premarket on record Q3 results and a demand-outstrips-supply-through-2030 outlook, lifting Micron and Samsung.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory, cooling, power and storage all beat in the same 24 hours — the AI-infrastructure demand chain has breadth, even if individual winners get sold after big runs.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: oil jumped after Yemen's Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery (550,000 barrels per day) with a missile; Saudi authorities had not confirmed the strike. Brent rose 1.8% to $115.90 and WTI 2.0% to $101.91 as of 0735 GMT. The official EIA inventory report lands at 10:30 a.m. ET today after API data showed a 2.03M-barrel draw.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-risk premium is back in crude hours before the Fed decision — single-source, unconfirmed on the strike itself, so treat the geopolitical leg as fragile even as the price move is real.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) pays Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Background: on Oct 1 the partnership issued 34.5M non-convertible Class A units at a fixed 9.25% annual distribution rate in an internal reorganization, and it now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after moving from NYSE on Oct 5. WTI back above $101 on the Saudi refinery headlines keeps the energy backdrop supportive with no company-specific catalyst.
